items.title: Google software engineer uses 48 AI agents to analyze NASA lidar data, discovers previously unmapped Maya pyramid in under 72 hours [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A Google software engineer employed 48 AI agents to analyze NASA lidar data covering about 1,200 square kilometers of jungle, leading to the discovery of a previously unregistered Maya archaeological site in Mexico within 72 hours. The AI agents identified structures including a pyramid, plaza, and possible water reservoir by filtering lidar images for man-made shapes and cross-referencing existing records. The engineer compiled a report with the help of AI agents, translated it into Spanish, and submitted it to Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH), which confirmed no prior registration of the site. While not yet officially verified, the site appears to be a small Classic period Maya civic center, potentially including a temple, ruler's courtyard, and rainwater reservoir.

items.title: Apple plans new Mac app Harbor to run local AI models and cluster multiple Macs via Thunderbolt 5 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Apple is developing a new Mac app called Harbor that enables users to run open-weight AI models locally on Apple silicon, turning Macs into private AI inference servers without sending data to the cloud. The app can connect multiple Macs over Thunderbolt 5 to pool unified memory, allowing larger models and higher concurrency than a single machine can handle alone. Harbor aims to simplify setup by automatically detecting devices and managing model downloads within the app, requiring no manual configuration or command-line expertise. Currently in private preview under Apple's Claris brand, Harbor is expected to launch publicly in the coming weeks or months.

items.title: Atuin launches Threads to sync and search AI agent sessions across machines with end-to-end encryption [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Atuin has introduced Threads, a feature that enables users to synchronize, search, and resume AI agent sessions across multiple devices while maintaining end-to-end encryption. This allows tasks started with one AI agent on a machine to be continued seamlessly on another, preserving all context and history. Threads supports several AI agents including Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Omp, and OpenCode, with more planned. The system builds on Atuin's encrypted sync engine and offers an opt-in model for capturing agent sessions, which can be hosted on Atuin's servers, self-hosted, or kept local. Additionally, Atuin's MCP tool allows agents to reference past sessions to improve continuity and efficiency in workflows.

items.title: Gilbert + Tobin explores AI integration to transform legal services and improve efficiency, says Partner and CEO Sam Nickless [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Gilbert + Tobin is investigating how artificial intelligence can reshape the legal industry by enhancing operational efficiency and client service. Sam Nickless, the firm's Partner and CEO, discusses the potential for AI to change the business model of law firms. The firm aims to leverage AI technologies to streamline legal processes and deliver better outcomes for clients, reflecting a broader trend of digital transformation in the legal sector.

items.title: DeepMind launches AlphaGenome 2 to predict DNA variant effects on gene expression across hundreds of human cell types using over 100 million single-cell profiles [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: DeepMind announced AlphaGenome 2, a next-generation model that predicts how DNA sequences and their variations impact specific human cell types, enhancing understanding of disease mechanisms. The model uses a conditional architecture to analyze DNA effects in individual cell types and states, improving variant effect predictions compared to previous models. Trained on more than 107 million single-cell profiles from 68 tissues, AlphaGenome 2 can predict gene expression, chromatin accessibility, histone modifications, and DNA methylation at the cell-type level. It adapts to new single-cell data without retraining and is available for non-commercial research via an API, with commercial access in private preview. By resolving activity in specialized cells rather than broad tissue averages, AlphaGenome 2 helps researchers identify disease-relevant genetic variants that may be missed by earlier models, potentially advancing studies in rare diseases, complex traits, and fundamental biology.

items.title: US charges three men with using AI to impersonate CEOs and attorneys in $129 million global fraud scheme [ ! ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Three foreign nationals were arrested and charged in the US for allegedly using AI to impersonate corporate executives and lawyers to defraud companies worldwide of over $129 million. The scheme, which occurred between 2024 and 2026, involved convincing employees to make large wire transfers to accounts across multiple countries before converting the funds into cryptocurrency to conceal their origin. Jacob Soall and Sharon Hazan were arrested in Spain, and Guy Sheetrit in the UK. The stolen funds came from various organizations including hospital systems, banks, mutual funds, and companies in the US and UK. US authorities highlighted the case as an example of how emerging technologies like AI can be exploited for large-scale fraud, and the suspects face charges including conspiracy to commit wire fraud, money laundering, and aggravated identity theft.

items.title: OpenAI offers free one-year ChatGPT Plus subscriptions to over 20,000 veterans and transitioning service members to support civilian career preparation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: OpenAI has provided more than 20,000 veterans and transitioning service members with a free one-year subscription to ChatGPT Plus. This initiative aims to assist them in preparing for careers outside the military by leveraging AI tools. Users have utilized ChatGPT Plus to enhance their job search, resume writing, interview preparation, and skill development as they transition to civilian life. The program reflects OpenAI's commitment to supporting veterans through technology access and career resources.

items.title: Databricks updates AI agent Genie to perform multi-step tasks and provide CEO Ali Ghodsi with unfiltered insights on company issues [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Databricks has released an enhanced version of its AI agent Genie, capable of completing complex, multi-step tasks autonomously by leveraging an ontology built from customer data on its platform. CEO Ali Ghodsi demonstrated how he uses Genie internally to analyze employee satisfaction surveys, evaluate sales pitches, and prepare for interviews, enabling him to access candid feedback and insights that might not reach him directly in a company of 12,000 employees. Ghodsi highlighted the challenge of maintaining direct communication in large organizations, referencing Dunbar's number to explain why employees may not share negative information with top executives. He believes AI agents like Genie can help leaders overcome this barrier by surfacing unvarnished truths and managing AI costs through Databricks' Unity Gateway, which controls usage and allows integration of less expensive models.

items.title: Report: Jensen Huang, Nvidia CEO, was targeted in a Chinese spy honeypot involving a former Singapore cloud executive linked to China's Ministry of State Security [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, was reportedly targeted in a Chinese intelligence honeypot operation involving Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, who US officials believe is an asset of China's Ministry of State Security. Nvidia's board has launched an investigation but stated there is no evidence that company secrets or national security were compromised. China has denied involvement, calling the allegations groundless, while US intelligence agencies have highlighted China's long history of economic espionage and use of honeypots to target key figures in technology and government. The case underscores ongoing concerns about Chinese intelligence efforts to infiltrate Silicon Valley and the global AI industry through sophisticated espionage tactics.

items.title: Anthropic and other AI researchers warn of accelerating AI development raising safety concerns
items.content_text: Anthropic and other AI safety researchers have expressed increased concern over the rapid acceleration of AI development, fearing that AI systems may soon surpass human control and pose significant risks. Recent reports indicate that AI capabilities are advancing faster than previously anticipated, intensifying worries about potential harm from unchecked AI progress. These concerns come amid a broader context of growing AI innovation and investment, with many startups rapidly gaining traction and valuations. The acceleration in AI development has also heightened the importance of AI infrastructure and security companies, as the frequency of AI-powered cyberattacks continues to rise, underscoring the need for robust safety measures.

items.title: Plurai raises $13M seed to improve AI agent reliability using simulation techniques from self-driving car development [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Plurai, a startup founded by former autonomous driving engineers, aims to enhance AI agent performance by creating digital twins of company systems and using simulations to prepare models for edge cases. The company raised $13 million in seed funding led by Team8 to develop this approach, which applies techniques from self-driving car training to AI agents operating in unpredictable environments. Plurai's platform maps possible agent workflows and generates synthetic data to evaluate and improve AI models, working alongside existing tools like Claude Code and Copilot. The startup also post-trains smaller, open-weight models tailored to customer needs, achieving comparable or better accuracy than mid-tier models at significantly lower costs. Investors highlight Plurai's focus on understanding failure modes and tuning models with synthetic data as a potential advantage for businesses managing AI expenses.

items.title: AI Code Rating launches a 3-character system to disclose AI usage and maintainer expertise in code repositories [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: AI Code Rating introduces a concise 3-character code to indicate how AI was used in a software repository and to rate the expertise of the maintainer responsible for the code. The system categorizes maintainers from Expert to Non-programmer based on their ability to write, understand, and review code without AI assistance. This rating aims to provide transparency about AI involvement and human oversight in code projects.

items.title: Helsing launches Clarity AI platform to prepare military target recommendations with mandatory human authorization and European control [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: German defense company Helsing has introduced Clarity, an AI platform that aggregates sensor data and intelligence to identify military targets and recommend weapons systems, emphasizing European sovereignty and human oversight. The system requires a human to authorize every strike, with each decision documented by the responsible individual's name. Helsing positions Clarity as a competitor to US vendors like Palantir and highlights its compliance with NATO standards and modular design for integration with various weapons systems. Clarity uses hundreds of specialized AI agents trained on operational, synthetic, and simulated data to analyze multiple sources in parallel, aiming to provide high-confidence target recommendations. However, experiences from conflicts in Iran, Gaza, and a near-miss involving China illustrate risks associated with rapid automation and data fusion, including shortened human review times and AI errors leading to dangerous misidentifications. These cases underscore challenges in verifying AI-generated intelligence and the potential consequences of overreliance on automated systems in military operations.

items.title: Google DeepMind mathematically verifies key cryptographic guarantees of Signal protocol using AI in a four-week project [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Google DeepMind researchers used an AI framework called AlphaProof Code to formally verify several critical cryptographic properties of the Signal protocol, which secures communications on apps like Signal, Google Messages, and WhatsApp. This four-week proof-of-concept project independently validates the protocol's security and demonstrates AI's potential to accelerate formal verification processes. The analysis confirmed the absence of new vulnerabilities in the verified portions and correctly identified known, fixed issues in older Signal versions. While the project did not cover the entire Signal app, it builds on prior formal verification efforts by the Signal Foundation and introduces a human-AI collaboration approach to improve verification efficiency. The researchers released their specifications and proofs to support further work, though the scalability and cost-effectiveness of AI-driven formal verification remain open questions for the broader tech industry.

items.title: The Information releases its 2026 list of 50 most promising startups, highlighting AI-driven security firms and Israeli founders [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The Information published its annual list of the 50 most promising startups for 2026, emphasizing the growing importance of AI in cybersecurity. The list features a new category dedicated to security startups, with three of the four highest-valued companies exceeding $1 billion in valuation and six led by Israeli founders known for success in this sector. The selection process relied on direct conversations with founders and investors and analysis of company revenue and growth, rather than AI tools. The list and a related conference call with several featured founders are available to Information subscribers.

items.title: Adobe unveils AI experiments at Max 2026 including 3D photo navigation, interactive AI character design, and automated photo editing tools [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Adobe showcased several experimental AI tools at its annual Max conference, including Project Screen Test for creating and interacting with AI characters through conversation, Project Sight Span for converting flat images into navigable 3D environments, and Project Rinse Repeat for copying photo edits across multiple subjects. These tools aim to enhance creative workflows by adding new dimensions to image and video editing, leveraging generative AI technology. Project Screen Test allows users to develop detailed AI character personalities by talking to them and directing their behavior, while Project Sight Span generates 3D scenes from any flat image, enabling users to explore beyond the original frame. Project Sound Bender offers AI-generated audio mixing synced to video clips, and Project Rinse Repeat automates applying edits like blemish removal or shadow adjustments across similar objects or people in photos. These projects are experimental previews and may be integrated into Adobe's Creative Cloud or Firefly platforms in the future, reflecting the company's focus on AI-driven creative tools.

items.title: Video explores AI's impact on music technology through Plato's Cave allegory and Star Trek themes [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The video "Vibecoding in Plato's Cave" examines how artificial intelligence is shaping music creation and perception. It connects these developments with philosophical concepts from Plato's Cave allegory and cultural references from the Star Trek universe, highlighting the interplay between technology, philosophy, and popular culture.

items.title: Forward Model launches MK1, a large language model trained to form investment judgments in financial markets [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Forward Model has developed MK1, a large language model specifically trained to analyze financial market data, including company filings, earnings calls, and news, to form investment judgments. Unlike previous quantitative models that focused on pattern recognition in prices and data, MK1 reads and interprets financial information to predict stock movements and explain its reasoning in plain language. The model was tested against leading AI models on unseen trading days to evaluate its predictive accuracy and judgment quality.

items.title: Anthropic shares IPO roadshow video revealing multi-chip strategy and compute multiplier approach for training and serving Claude AI [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Anthropic released a video as part of its IPO roadshow that details its approach to training and serving its AI model Claude across multiple chip families, including AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, and AMD GPUs. The company highlighted its early bet on a multi-chip strategy, which allows it to run AI models on different hardware platforms efficiently, and its discovery of compute multipliers that enhance effective compute capacity. Co-founder Tom Brown explained that Anthropic's software stack supports multiple chip types, enabling rapid deployment on new hardware such as AMD GPUs with minimal human intervention. The company emphasized that compute multipliers multiply the effective compute available, allowing for more efficient training or more intelligent models. Anthropic believes this approach creates a competitive advantage and anticipates further acceleration through recursive self-improvement, where Claude could autonomously discover new compute multipliers.

items.title: Analysis: AI progress largely driven by persistent research and continuous refinement rather than sudden breakthroughs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Recent advancements in artificial intelligence have resulted primarily from sustained effort and ongoing improvements instead of abrupt innovations. This steady persistence in research and development has enabled gradual enhancement of AI capabilities over time.
